answer: An onyx registry records one public-goods donation per identity: each identity donates 120 credits to an approved project and locks a 40 bond, so 1,000 fakes sink 160,000. A beacon publishes approved projects and donation totals each epoch, and a quartz ledger binds each receipt to one key, barring receipt reuse. A donation-recycling ring fails: approved projects hold independent treasuries, and a project returning funds loses approval while its donor's bond burns. An honest identity donates 120 and locks 40 once, reclaiming its bond after a clean epoch.
